subject: Nanotechnology
title: Mie Scattering from Nanoparticles
description: A quick win: understand Mie Scattering from Nanoparticles.

hook.text: A gold nanoparticle looks red — not because of pigment, but because it scatters green light and transmits red.

buildup.text: Mie theory describes how spherical particles scatter light — the scattered color depends on size and material.

discovery.text: Particles near the wavelength of light show strong resonances — specific sizes scatter specific colors intensely.

twist.text: Rayleigh scattering applies only to tiny particles — Mie theory covers the full range but is far more complex.

climax.text: Mie scattering explains sunset colors, paint pigments, and the design of nano-optical antennas.

punchline.text: Size sets the color when nanoparticles meet light.

quiz.question: Why does a gold nanoparticle appear red?
options: Gold atoms naturally emit red light
It scatters green light and transmits red, governed by Mie scattering resonance
It absorbs all light except ultraviolet
